Should Investors Bet on Diodes After the ElevATE Acquisition?
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 7:45 AM PDT 3 min read
Diodes Incorporated DIOD has strengthened its growth profile with the acquisition of ElevATE Semiconductor, expanding its presence in the automated test equipment (ATE) market. The deal adds higher-margin analog and mixed-signal products to Diodes' portfolio and is likely to support its revenue and margin recovery.
ElevATE Deal Expands DIOD's Growth Opportunities
Diodes completed the $250 million all-cash acquisition on Aug. 27. ElevATE develops highly integrated, low-power analog and mixed-signal ICs used in semiconductor test equipment.
Management expects ElevATE to contribute about $50 million in revenues during the first 12 months following the acquisition. Thereafter, it is projected to deliver a revenue compound annual growth rate of more than 20% over the next four years.
The buyout also gives Diodes greater exposure to semiconductor testing, where increasing chip complexity across AI, automotive and industrial applications is driving demand for more advanced test solutions.
Higher-Margin Mix Could Aid Profitability
One of the key attractions of the transaction is ElevATE's profitability profile. It generates gross margins significantly above Diodes' corporate average, and management expects the acquisition to be immediately accretive to revenues, gross margin and earnings per share. A greater contribution from higher-margin analog and mixed-signal products could therefore accelerate Diodes' margin recovery as factory utilization improves and demand conditions normalize.
The acquisition comes against a backdrop of improving operating momentum for Diodes. Second-quarter 2026 revenues increased 21.7% year over year to $445.5 million, while gross margin expanded 160 basis points to 33.1%.
Automotive revenues increased 37%, computing revenues rose 33%, supported by AI data-center demand, and industrial revenues advanced 24%. Non-GAAP earnings more than doubled to 70 cents per share.
These trends suggest that Diodes is benefiting from a broader recovery across several important end markets, providing a more supportive backdrop for integrating ElevATE.
Diodes has gained 88.4% over the past year compared with the industry's growth of 35.9%, lagging peers like FormFactor, Inc. FORM and ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ASX. FORM has gained 251.9%, while ASX is up 307.1% over this period.
The ElevATE buyout strengthens Diodes' exposure to higher-growth and higher-margin semiconductor markets and the ATE market while complementing improving trends in automotive, industrial and AI-related computing demand. The deal could also help Diodes achieve its longer-term targets of $2 billion in annual revenues and more than $4 in non-GAAP EPS, providing a favorable setup for continued earnings expansion. Consequently, the stock appears to be a solid investment option in the volatile market.

Should Investors Bet on Diodes After the ElevATE Acquisition?
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 7:45 AM PDT 3 min read
Diodes Incorporated DIOD has strengthened its growth profile with the acquisition of ElevATE Semiconductor, expanding its presence in the automated test equipment (ATE) market. The deal adds higher-margin analog and mixed-signal products to Diodes' portfolio and is likely to support its revenue and margin recovery.
ElevATE Deal Expands DIOD's Growth Opportunities
Diodes completed the $250 million all-cash acquisition on Aug. 27. ElevATE develops highly integrated, low-power analog and mixed-signal ICs used in semiconductor test equipment.
Management expects ElevATE to contribute about $50 million in revenues during the first 12 months following the acquisition. Thereafter, it is projected to deliver a revenue compound annual growth rate of more than 20% over the next four years.
The buyout also gives Diodes greater exposure to semiconductor testing, where increasing chip complexity across AI, automotive and industrial applications is driving demand for more advanced test solutions.
Higher-Margin Mix Could Aid Profitability
One of the key attractions of the transaction is ElevATE's profitability profile. It generates gross margins significantly above Diodes' corporate average, and management expects the acquisition to be immediately accretive to revenues, gross margin and earnings per share. A greater contribution from higher-margin analog and mixed-signal products could therefore accelerate Diodes' margin recovery as factory utilization improves and demand conditions normalize.
The acquisition comes against a backdrop of improving operating momentum for Diodes. Second-quarter 2026 revenues increased 21.7% year over year to $445.5 million, while gross margin expanded 160 basis points to 33.1%.
Automotive revenues increased 37%, computing revenues rose 33%, supported by AI data-center demand, and industrial revenues advanced 24%. Non-GAAP earnings more than doubled to 70 cents per share.
These trends suggest that Diodes is benefiting from a broader recovery across several important end markets, providing a more supportive backdrop for integrating ElevATE.
Diodes has gained 88.4% over the past year compared with the industry's growth of 35.9%, lagging peers like FormFactor, Inc. FORM and ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ASX. FORM has gained 251.9%, while ASX is up 307.1% over this period.
The ElevATE buyout strengthens Diodes' exposure to higher-growth and higher-margin semiconductor markets and the ATE market while complementing improving trends in automotive, industrial and AI-related computing demand. The deal could also help Diodes achieve its longer-term targets of $2 billion in annual revenues and more than $4 in non-GAAP EPS, providing a favorable setup for continued earnings expansion. Consequently, the stock appears to be a solid investment option in the volatile market.
